registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permissible for SL companies if the registered office provides a physical address for correspondence and meets the requirements of the Registro Mercantil; commonly accepted for administrative compliance
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low likelihood for routine incorporations; physical verification may occur during regulatory inspections but is not standard for pre-incorporation due diligence

3,000 EUR statutory minimum plus bank fees

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1/2010, de 5 de marzo, de Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada (LSRL), Articles 1-4 (formation), 5-6 (capital), 7-10 (shareholders) and general provisions of the Código de Comercio
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum capital of 3,000 euros pursuant to Article 5 LSRL; must be paid in full upon incorporation or in installments with proof of payment submitted to notary and registry; no escrow account required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors of [Company Name] resolves unanimously: (1) the sole shareholder subscribes to the full share capital of 3,000 euros by subscribing to all shares; (2) the registered office is adopted at the address specified in the Articles; (3) [Name] is appointed Managing Director, [Name] as Director, and [Name] as Secretary. The Managing Director is authorized to execute all filings with the Registro Mercantil and to open bank accounts. This resolution is adopted on [date] and remains in force until further resolution.

Sole shareholder identification and share subscription proof

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Agencia Española de Protección del Medio Ambiente y Medio Marino (current: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y la Despoblación del Territorio)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable; inspection and testing services generate no wastewater, VOCs or regulated emissions

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from local fire department, structural load inspection if premises require, and workplace safety clearance from labor authorities

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT), official portal https://www.agenciatributaria.gob.es/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign entities register with AEAT to obtain NIF (CIF for companies) via online portal submission of application form, corporate documents, passport copies, proof of Spanish address or representative, and tax identification details; processing typically 10-15 business days with possible in-person verification at AEAT offices.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box elections available; hybrid mismatch and reverse hybrid rules under EU Anti-Tax Avoidance Directive (ATAD) apply to certain structures; SL entities classified as tax-transparent for corporate income tax purposes at entity level with no pass-through election option.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 30,000 EUR annual taxable turnover threshold triggering mandatory registration (or 10,000 EUR for intra-EU distance sales under certain conditions)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory facturación electrónica for all B2B and B2C transactions above specified thresholds via AEAT-certified platforms or API integration; real-time fiscal reporting and digital stamping required for large taxpayers with full XML/EDiFICE compliance and immediate clearance obligations.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to goods physically exported outside the EU with proof of exit from EU territory; offshore services to non-EU clients qualify under specific territorial rules with documentary substantiation of non-EU performance and payment.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or Air Waybill
Inward Remittance Certificate or proof of non-EU payment
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Penalties up to 100% of evaded VAT plus statutory interest; retrospective clawback of zero-rated VAT claims if export not evidenced, goods reimported, or fraudulent documentation detected with potential criminal referral.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain), acting within the Eurosystem and under the monetary policy framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); foreign-exchange monitoring, statistical declarations of economic transactions with non-residents, and foreign-investment filings are administered jointly by Banco de España and the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCOMIN) of the Ministry of Economy, Trade and Business; AML/CFT supervision is exercised by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales e Infracciones Monetarias).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible as a floating international reserve currency. Spain maintains no exchange controls on either the current or the capital account: the EU free-movement-of-capital regime (TFEU Article 63), implemented nationally by Law 19/2003 of 4 July on capital movements and economic transactions with foreign countries and by Royal Decree 1816/1991, permits unrestricted collection from non-resident clients, free conversion of FX receipts, and unrestricted dividend/profit remittance. A cross-border dividend paid by an SL is freely remitted abroad, subject only to a 19% non-resident withholding tax (reduced or eliminated under an applicable tax treaty). The operative statutory obligations for a medium-sized inspection/QC agency are: (i) statistical declaration to Banco de España of each non-resident transaction equal to or above EUR 50,000 (Form N-1, due by the 15th calendar day of the month following the transaction); and (ii) post-closing foreign-direct-investment declaration to DGCOMIN for non-resident participations reaching 10% or conferring control, pursuant to Royal Decree 571/2023. The post-2020 investment-screening mechanism (introduced by Royal Decree-Law 34/2020 and integrated into Law 19/2003) requires prior authorisation for non-EU/EFTA acquirers of 10% or more of strategic assets in defence, dual-use technology, critical infrastructure, energy, telecoms, media, health, and personal-data platforms; an ISIC 7120 factory-inspection and pre-shipment QC agency is not a screened sector in its standard configuration, but a diligence note should verify that its client portfolio does not incidentally expose it to critical-infrastructure facilities or sensitive data.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or conversion obligation exists under Spanish or Eurosystem law. There is no statutory repatriation period, no mandatory conversion ratio, no requirement to route export/service proceeds through a designated official channel, and no currency retention ceiling for the SL. The SL may invoice and hold receivables in EUR or any convertible currency, settle through foreign accounts, and freely hedge the resulting exposure. The only compliance duties are: (i) Banco de España Form N-1 declaration for each receipt/payment of EUR 50,000 or more (transaction-by-transaction statistical reporting); and (ii) retention of the supporting commercial invoice, purchase order, inspection report, and SWIFT confirmation in order to validate the declaration and the VAT reverse-charge treatment of cross-border B2B inspection services. If the payer is in a currency-restricted Latin American jurisdiction (e.g., Argentina), any payment limitation arises from the payer's domestic regime, not from Spanish FX law, and the Spanish bank will not impose separate surrender requirements.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-to-High as an auxiliary collections and FX-conversion layer; Low as the sole or primary treasury rail for the SL. Wise Europe S.A. (an electronic money institution authorised by the National Bank of Belgium and passporting into Spain under PSD2; commercial distribution via Wise Spain, S.L.U. registered with Banco de España) offers a EUR IBAN, multi-currency balances (USD, MXN, BRL, ARS, CLP, COP, PEN), and mid-market conversion, which is commercially efficient for collecting pre-shipment inspection fees from Latin American and US principals in their local currencies and converting to EUR. Legal constraints: an EMI is not a credit institution and cannot grant overdrafts, issue letters of credit, arrange documentary collections, or provide derivative hedging; funds are safeguarded in segregated accounts but are not covered by the Spanish Deposit Guarantee Fund (FGD); a UK-only licensed EMI without a valid EEA passport may not lawfully service Spanish residents after Brexit. Treasury policy for the SL should therefore maintain a Tier-1 commercial bank as the settlement bank of record (for Form N-1 reporting, intercompany capital injections, documentary trade, and any ISDA/CMOF hedging), while Wise can be used as an expedited collection/disbursement layer for low-value recurring payments.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: No statutory mandate requires physical attendance by directors or shareholders: Law 10/2010 on the prevention of money laundering permits non-face-to-face identification through a recognised qualified electronic signature (DNIe/NIE digital certificate) or a secure audio-video identification procedure embedded in the bank's approved AML policy. In practice, Tier-1 Spanish banks accept remote onboarding of the SL's director and ultimate beneficial owner when the following are supplied in electronic form: notarised and apostilled passport and NIE certificate, certified Spanish or English translation, public deed of incorporation, current transcript from the Registro Mercantil, NIF certificate, audited or financial statements if available, a signed economic-purpose questionnaire, and a live video call with passport display. Account opening completes within 3 to 10 business days. A physical interview at branch or consulate will in practice be required if: (i) the UBO resides in a non-OECD or FATF-monitored jurisdiction; (ii) the bank's risk-model flags the payer countries (e.g., certain Latin American jurisdictions with capital controls or sanctions complexity); or (iii) projected turnover exceeds approximately EUR 1 million in year one. A director holding an EU passport and a current NIE/TIE is virtually never required to appear; a non-resident director without NIE should apply for one before opening to shorten the KYC timeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director/UBO lacking a Spanish tax residency or NIE, and/or UBO resident in a FATF-monitored or enhanced-due-diligence jurisdiction, causing automatic high-risk classification of the SL at onboarding.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarised and apostilled passport; current NIE/TIE certificate or proof of NIE application; source-of-wealth statement covering the prior three years (tax returns or audited financial statements of the parent); group corporate-scheme chart evidencing the full UBO chain to the natural person; bank reference letter from the UBO's home institution; and a signed AML questionnaire explaining that the account serves solely the collection of factory-inspection fees and the payment of operational expenses.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Expected cross-border inflows (USD, EUR, and Latin American currencies) that are disproportionate to a low-risk services company, especially repeated credits at or above EUR 50,000 in the first six months, raising an unstructured-flow flag.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed master service agreements and purchase orders for each principal; dated pre-shipment inspection reports and quality certificates; commercial invoices matched to each inbound wire; the SL's registered-office lease, payroll records, and professional liability insurance as evidence of real operations; and a counterparty-by-counterparty cash-flow forecast demonstrating the commercial rationality of the projected volume.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment origin different from the invoiced beneficiary (e.g., a Hong Kong or Miami trading company paying for inspections of goods in Spain), or instructions to route funds onward to third-party factories, creating an agency/pass-through pattern that resembles layering.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Written tri-partite or agency agreement establishing the principal-agent relationship; matched chain of invoice to purchase order to shipment-linked inspection certificate; subcontractor agreements and commercial due-diligence files on each ultimate payee; certificate from the Registro Mercantil and the beneficial-ownership register (RLM) confirming control of the SL; and a policy note explaining the commercial necessity for split payments (commission retention versus factory disbursement).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Rapid inbound capital injection from a foreign parent followed within days by outward disbursements to non-resident suppliers, flagged as potential layering or round-tripping.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Capital increase or incorporation deed registered with the Registro Mercantil; shareholders' ledger (libro registro de socios) showing the subscription; audited financial statements of the parent evidencing the source of funds; board resolution stating that proceeds fund working capital and no local financing is available; a Treasury cash-flow forecast; and copies of the timely filed Banco de España Form N-1/N-4 declarations showing that the operation was transparently reported.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital injections from a non-resident parent or shareholder must be executed by SWIFT MT103 (or a SEPA credit transfer when the investor is EEA-resident) to the SL's Tier-1 IBAN, with Field 70 remittance information stating 'Suscripcion de capital social - Escritura [date]/[notary number]' and referencing the investor's corporate identifier and the SL's NIF. The beneficiary bank will require the notarial deed, the updated Registro Mercantil transcript, and the shareholders' ledger to classify the credit as foreign direct investment rather than revenue or loan. For injections of EUR 50,000 or more, the SL reports the transaction to Banco de España on Form N-1 by the 15th of the following month; if the non-resident's participation reaches 10% or effective control, a post-closing direct-investment declaration must be filed with DGCOMIN through the electronic Declaraciones de Inversiones Exteriores portal (generally within one month of the notarial deed). Where funds are injected as a shareholder loan instead of equity, a written loan agreement with arm's-length interest is mandatory, the credit is declared on Form N-4 (loans and deposits with non-residents), and the interest is subject to 19% withholding unless reduced by treaty. Prior authorisation under the 2020 screening regime is not triggered by a standard ISIC 7120 inspection/QC agency; a pre-transaction screen is nonetheless recommended when any client contract touches critical infrastructure or defence-related goods.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For domestic and EEA suppliers/subcontractors, the SL uses SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant (TARGET2) from its Tier-1 IBAN with same-day or next-day settlement at zero or minimal cost. For non-EEA counterparties (Asian or Latin American factories), the SL clears through SWIFT MT103 via the bank's nostro/correspondent network, subject to EU and OFAC sanctions pre-screening and AML travel-rule checks; each debit is supported by the commercial invoice and, where contractually relevant, the inspection certificate. When a principal or export customer requires secured payment terms, the SL may open irrevocable commercial letters of credit under UCP600/eUCP (MT700) or use documentary collections under URC522, both of which Spanish Tier-1 banks issue natively; the inspection report is routinely listed as a required document in such instruments. For low-value recurring disbursements into Latin American local-clearing systems, Wise can execute local instant rails at mid-market conversion, but every Wise payment must be separately documented with invoice, purchase order, and proof of delivery to prevent pass-through flags; SEPA Direct Debit (Core) can be used for recurring collections from EEA principals, while non-EEA principals pay by wire or Wise balance.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Over-the-counter outright FX forward (compra/venta de divisas a plazo) with a Banco de España-supervised credit institution under an ISDA 2002 or CMOF (Contrato Marco de Operaciones Financieras) master agreement; available in EUR/USD, EUR/MXN, EUR/BRL and other freely convertible pairs with tenors typically up to 18 months for a non-financial corporate.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for restricted or illiquid Latin American currencies (ARS, COP, PEN, CLP) under which the Spanish bank cash-settles the difference in EUR against the reference or central-bank fixing, as physical delivery of those currencies to the SL is barred or economically impractical.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) and European-style FX options (call/put on EUR/USD or EUR/LatAm crosses) used to hedge firm multi-quarter inspection programmes where client commitments create a scheduled currency cash-flow; all derivative products require MiFID II appropriateness assessment and are permitted for risk-hedging purposes only, not for speculative trading by an SME.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Accounts Deposit (Depósito de Cuentas Anuales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil); summary published in BORME
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Ordinary General Meeting must approve accounts within 6 months of fiscal year-end (by June 30); deposit within 1 month of approval (by July 31 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure (cierre registral) blocking all further corporate filings and certificates until deposit; ICAC fines for non-deposit or formal deficiencies from EUR 1,200 up to EUR 60,000; adverse good-standing certificates for banking counterparties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, Modelo 200)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months and 25 days after the tax year-end; for a December 31 year-end the deadline is July 25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge per Art. 27 LGT: 5% of net tax due plus 1% per additional calendar month (capped at 20%), plus arrears interest; inaccurate filing sanction 15%-50%; material omissions up to 100%; non-filing minimum penalties begin at approximately EUR 300

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 30 following the calendar year-end (annual recap of quarterly Modelo 303 filings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Informative declaration penalties per Art. 198 LGT: EUR 300 per omitted or incorrect data item, minimum EUR 500, maximum EUR 20,000; late VAT surcharge 5%-20% plus interest if accompanied by payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Withholdings Summary Return (Modelo 190 — employee and professional IRPF withholdings)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 31 following the calendar year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 300 per omitted or incorrect certificate or amount, minimum EUR 500, maximum EUR 20,000; unpaid withheld tax triggers surcharges and 100% sanctions for false data

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By February 28 following the calendar year-end; filing threshold: aggregate annual transactions with a single counterparty exceeding EUR 3,005.06
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: EUR 300 per omitted or incorrect counterparty record, minimum EUR 500, maximum EUR 20,000; special 2% charge on erroneously omitted or incorrectly declared aggregate amounts

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Confirmation (Declaración de Titularidad Real / UBO form)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Mercantile Registry, transmitted to the Central Register of Ultimate Beneficial Owners (Registro Central de Titularidades Reales, Ministry of Justice)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 10 days of any change in ultimate beneficial ownership; annual confirmation integrated with the deposit of annual accounts (by July 31 for a calendar year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Law 10/2010 AML regime: minor infringement fines up to EUR 90,000; serious up to EUR 150,000; very serious from EUR 150,001 up to 2% of own funds with public censure; registry filings for share transfers barred until UBO updated

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Legalization of Corporate Books (Legalización de Libros de Contabilidad — Journal, Inventories, Annual Accounts Book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months following the fiscal year-end (by April 30 for a December 31 year-end)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Loss of evidentiary value in court and arbitration; tax penalty per Art. 200 LGT of 2% of net turnover (minimum EUR 1,500) for irregular or non-legalized accounting; ICAC fines up to EUR 60,000

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory independent audit is compulsory (Art. 263 LSC) when at least two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at the balance sheet date for two consecutive fiscal years: total assets above EUR 2,850,000; net turnover above EUR 5,700,000; average number of employees above 50. Audit also mandatory for listed or multilateral-trading securities issuers, financial and insurance entities, and group consolidating companies; all other SLs may voluntarily audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (Plan General Contable, RD 1514/2007 as amended by RD 1/2021) for medium and large companies; SME PGC (RD 1515/2007 as amended) for eligible small companies (assets not exceeding EUR 4,000,000; turnover not exceeding EUR 8,000,000; employees not exceeding 50). Consolidated accounts of listed groups apply IFRS-EU; individual statutory accounts apply local GAAP (PGC).

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers in an SL must be executed before a notary, notified to the company, and entered in the Register of Members before they are opposable to the company; the transferee cannot exercise voting or dividend rights until inscription. The UBO declaration must be updated with the Mercantile Registry within 10 days of any shareholding change and reconfirmed each year together with the deposit of annual accounts; the operator providing on-site inspection services does not alter this protocol as the company is a standard non-regulated SL.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Inventory and Annual Accounts Book (Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales)

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for the first two tax periods of a newly created Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada meeting the conditions of Art. 29.1 LIS; R&D and technological innovation tax credits under Art. 35 LIS; tax deductions for intangible fixed assets and anti-layoff employment incentives; no expatriate or notional interest deduction for this audit-firm model unless specifically legislated.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no statutory time-bar under Art. 26 LIS); offset is subject to annual quantitative limits based on turnover, not to a five-year expiry.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically through the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT; mandatory online submission for legal persons.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly prepayments via Form 202 for taxpayers with positive taxable bases and sufficient prior-year benchmark.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end: for a calendar year ending 31 December, the filing deadline is 25 July; non-calendar year-ends follow the 25th day of the seventh month after year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Spanish taxpayer identification number (NIF) and full legal name of the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The entity must use its Spanish NIF; no foreign registration number can be substituted. Non-resident directors must ensure the NIF is active and validated before filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start and end dates of the financial/tax year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For an SL, the fiscal year is normally the calendar year unless otherwise adopted by by-law amendment; non-resident shareholders cannot unilaterally change the period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: National Classification of Economic Activities code: 7120 for technical testing and analysis (ISIC 7120).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The CNAE code must reflect the actual inspection/QC activity; using a service category inconsistent with commercial reality triggers risk reclassification.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting profit/loss before corporation tax from the financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts must reconcile with the statutory audit file presented to the commercial registry; foreign tax adjustments are not made in this field.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Permanent and temporary corrections to accounting result under Arts. 11 to 16 LIS (depreciation, provisions, valuations, non-deductible expenses).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-deductible cross-border expenses, such as unsupported management fees or intra-group royalties lacking substance, must be added back here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 / Compensación de bases imponibles negativas
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of prior-year negative taxable bases.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the amount of prior losses being offset; the offset is unlimited in time but subject to the legal caps for entities with large turnover; records of the loss inventory must be retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Resulting taxable base after adjustments, offsets, and allocations.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For non-resident-owned SLs, any base generated through deemed-domicile or controlled-foreign-corporation corrections of foreign operations must be included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applying the general rate (or reduced rate) to the taxable base; includes calculation of the minimum tax amount for large entities.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident activity does not alter the statutory rate; the 15% new-co rate is only available where the SL has active economic activity and meets the corporate substance criteria.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Domestic and treaty-related deductions, overpayments, available credits such as R&D, reinvestment, double taxation relief.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax credits must be supported by contemporaneous documentation; foreign withholding tax credits are applied here if a TRC and income certification are attached.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Amounts withheld from customers or from Spanish payers plus quarterly instalment payments already made.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident clients without a Spanish permanent establishment are not subject to Spanish withholding on service fees; enter only Spanish source withholdings.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax due (positive) or refund (negative) after application of all credits, withholdings, and instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a refund, the SL must have the bank account verified; refund requests attract AEAT review of real economic activity in Spain.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior notification produces a 5% surcharge of the tax due if within three months, 10% within six months, 15% within twelve months, 20% thereafter; late-payment interest under Art. 26 LGT accrues; inaccurate or incomplete returns trigger penalty of 50% to 150% of the full omitted amount, reduced only by voluntary correction. Criminal consequences apply when the omitted tax exceeds EUR 120,000.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 19% for dividends distributed by the Spanish SL to a non-resident shareholder without a permanent establishment in Spain; 0% available under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive (RDL 5/2004 Art. 14.2) where a qualified EU/EEA parent holds at least 5% of the capital.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To apply a reduced DTA rate or exemption, the beneficial owner must submit an official Certificate of Tax Residence (TRC) for the relevant fiscal year, provide the payment documentation to the Spanish paying entity before the distribution, and, for refunds, file Form 210 or Form 216 with the AEAT within one month of the payment date; the payer must also include the transaction in the Form 294/296 withholding summaries.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: 19% statutory withholding, with treaty rates usually 5% or 10% depending on IP type and ownership; 0% for EU-qualifying companies under the Interest and Royalties Directive if the recipient has 25% direct capital relationship for an uninterrupted two-year period. Interest: 19% statutory withholding; most Spanish DTAs reduce the rate to 10% for portfolio debt and 0% for financial institutions or government entities; arm's-length test and lender substance review apply.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 250,000 per annum and related party for the provision of services triggers Local File documentation obligations; a Master File is mandatory where the consolidated worldwide turnover of the group is EUR 75 million or more; documentation must be prepared before the Form 200 filing deadline and produced to the tax administration within 30 days of formal notice.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Spain does not maintain offshore Economic Substance Regulations as in low-tax jurisdictions, but the doctrine of economic substance is embedded in Spanish GAAR (Art. 15 and 16 LGT), in the OECD Multilateral Instrument principal purpose test, and in the residence rules: an SL is a Spanish resident if it is incorporated under Spanish law or has its registered office, place of effective management, or board decision-making in Spain. Passive invoice-processing arrangements, staffless offices, and management overridden by foreign parent are attacked as artificial, denied treaty benefits, and subjected to 150% penalty plus interest.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate omission or understatement of fees from factory inspections, quality audits, and on-site testing through cash collection, second-set of books, or false invoices from shell subcontractors.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative penalty of 50% to 150% of the omitted tax plus late-payment interest; criminal penalty under Art. 305 of the Spanish Criminal Code of imprisonment from one to five years and a fine of up to six times the defrauded amount where the applicable tax loss exceeds EUR 120,000 per tax period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors, managers, and de facto officers who participated in the evasion can be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax debt under Art. 42 LGT; if prosecuted, the criminal court can order travel bans, passport seizure, and disqualification from serving as directors for the term of the sentence.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Registering an SL without real business activity, employees, or premises, and using it solely to invoice inspection and QC fees to foreign related parties while the actual services and control are performed outside Spain.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Fiscal simulation in Art. 16 LGT permits full recharacterization of the transaction, disallowance of expenses, denial of DTA benefits, and application of a penalty of 150% on the additional assessment; recognition as a sham company may also trigger civil insolvency liabilities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil will be pierced to hold directors personally liable for the tax arrears and penalties; criminal charges for fraud or false accounting may carry disqualification for managing Spanish companies for up to ten years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging non-arm's-length management fees, technology royalties, or inflated purchase invoices to or from foreign shareholders; failing to prepare Local/Master File; engaging in profit-stripping where interest, royalties, or service fees leave Spain without economic value.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AEAT adjustment to the arm's-length price under Art. 18 LIS, with 15% surcharge on the corrected valuation base; failure to produce TP documentation triggers a separate penalty of EUR 1,050 to EUR 5,000 per item and late-payment interest; overall penalty can reach 150% of the deficiency if intent is shown.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Administrators who knowingly approve inflated cross-border charges can be declared jointly liable for the tax deficiency; criminal tax fraud liability arises if the adjusted tax plus excluded costs exceeds the criminal threshold and the directors signed false informational filings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Disguising dividend distributions as tax-deductible interest or royalties through artificial debt participation structures, back-to-back loans, or service contracts with tax-haven recipients; failing to withhold 19% on actual dividends, interest, or royalties paid to non-residents.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The payer remains liable for the unwithheld amount under Art. 23.3 LGT, plus penalty of 50% to 150% of the amount not withheld; requalification of disguised interest as dividends denies the deduction and subjects the payment to 19% WHT.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false loan or royalty documentation are personally liable for the withholding debt and face criminal sanction for tax evasion; a court may impose temporary suspension of professional licenses and a travel ban during criminal investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: For an inspection and testing agency, accepting unexplained cash or structured wire transfers from non-resident principals, ignoring beneficial ownership requests, or failing to conduct know-your-customer checks under Spanish AML Law 10/2010.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Serious AML infringement: fines from EUR 30,001 to EUR 150,000; very serious infringement: fines from EUR 150,001 to EUR 5 million or 10% of annual turnover; in cases of laundering connection, criminal penalties of imprisonment up to six years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors of the SL are personally and severally liable for AML fines when order or consent is proven; susceptibility to travel bans, asset embargo, and prohibition on performing commercial functions in regulated sectors accompanies the economic sanction.
